A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Attention Surgery work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench and VBench-2.0 evaluations, component ablations, generated-video examples, and a human study comprising 562 paired comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation experiments and the human study, and additionally reports mobile latency and memory-traffic measurements.

M1.justification: The hybrid attention formula, uniform token selection, polynomial feature maps, distillation objectives, block-rate optimization, and fine-tuning procedure are retained. Notation edits do not establish an architectural or algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Training datasets, VBench, VBench-2.0, and human-study coverage remain unchanged. New computational tests extend coverage to variable video durations and longer sequences, including memory measurements at 81–141 frames. These extend resource-testing scenarios, without adding long-video generation-quality evaluations.

E2.justification: The comparator coverage substantially expands: Table 1 adds reported VBench scores for STA, VSA, and SANA-Video; new Table 4 includes CogVideoX-1.5 in the VBench-2.0 comparison; and appendix Table 8 compares against HedgeHog linear attention. MVDiT merely renames the earlier Wu et al. mobile entry.

E3.justification: v3 adds a distinct hardware-evaluation protocol using QNN on Snapdragon8-Gen4, measuring single-block latency and memory reads/writes alongside FLOPs. Duration sweeps and frame-count tests broaden evaluation beyond the earlier quality and FLOPs comparisons. Existing benchmark settings and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 1 and appendix A.3 add resource-scaling analyses that examine increasing video length, including out-of-memory behavior. The original distillation, block-selection, loss-function, feature-map complexity, and qualitative analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions average ablation results across the same four training checkpoints. Neither adds repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty reporting for the new hardware measurements.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises Wan2.1* and 15×R2 total scores from 82.47 and 82.40 to 83.10 and 83.21 without explaining the revisions; Figure 7 also changes. New results include approximately 6× faster inference per block at 7.5 seconds and mobile memory comparisons. Detailed appendix VBench-2.0 results remain unchanged, but new Table 4 conflicts with Table 11: Wan physics is 53.8 versus 53.3, and hybrid human fidelity is 78.9 versus 79.0.

T1.justification: The attention equations, feature-map construction, loss definitions, and knapsack formulation retain their mathematical substance. Dimension notation and equation formatting are simplified; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the claim of the first competitive sub-quadratic video diffusion models and its explicit 40% FLOPs-reduction statement, emphasizing competitive quality and improved mobile scaling instead. The introduction softens the assertion that no competitive linear-attention video model exists. The three main methodological contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new duration-scaling results as implying larger efficiency advantages at higher resolutions. Related work replaces the explicit worst-case quadratic qualification with an explanation emphasizing attention to all tokens and long-range dependencies, although Section 3.2 still describes the quadratic component.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link, identifies QNN and Snapdragon8-Gen4 for profiling, and newly documents randomized presentation order in the existing human study. This disclosure does not establish a changed study procedure. Appendix A.1 retains the optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes, sampler, precision, and training iterations.

R1.justification: Related work adds SANA-Video, Compact Attention, SpargeAttn, trainable sparse attention, sliding tile attention, and an Open-Sora reference. Positioning shifts toward lightweight conversion and all-token attention, replacing explicit superiority statements over Efficient-vDiT and M4V with broader comparisons.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to the abstract, parts of the introduction and related work, and small explanatory edits. A computational-efficiency paragraph and mobile-memory appendix subsection are added, while the overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains FLOPs and latency panels; Table 1 expands; new VBench-2.0 summary and mobile-memory tables appear; and Figure 7 is redrawn with revised labels. Several retained displays move, but the original ablation displays and appendix video grids remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Mobile measurements provide practical support for the central efficiency argument beyond v1's FLOPs comparisons, and newer baselines and moderated novelty claims improve positioning. The gain is limited by block-level rather than end-to-end timing, unexplained VBench score revisions, and inconsistencies between the new VBench-2.0 summary and retained appendix.
